7
Objects P and Q form an isolated system.
Object P has mass 6.0 kg and is moving at a speed of 3.0 m s–1.
Object Q has mass 2.0 kg and is moving at a speed of 4.2 m s–1 at an angle of 35° to the path
of P.
Q
2.0 kg
35°
4.2 m s–1
P
6.0 kg
3.0 m s–1
Objects P and Q collide and stick together.
What is the magnitude of the component of the final momentum of the combined objects in the
original direction of P?
A
9.6 kg m s–1
B
11 kg m s–1
C
13 kg m s–1
D
25 kg m s–1

hints: Notice the original direction of P is horizontal to the right, while Q at $4.2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is moving down and to the left at $35^{\circ}$ to the horizontal.
Recall that for an isolated system the vector component of total momentum along one direction is conserved, so resolve Q's momentum $m_Qv_Q$ with $\cos35^{\circ}$ for the horizontal part.
Compare the signs: P contributes $+6.0 \times 3.0$ and Q contributes a negative $2.0 \times 4.2\cos35^{\circ}$ along P's direction, then add them for the final combined momentum component.
walkthrough: Take the original direction of P as positive x. P's momentum is fully along x: $p_P = m_P v_P = 6.0 \times 3.0 = 18.0 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
Q's magnitude of momentum is $p_Q = m_Q v_Q = 2.0 \times 4.2 = 8.4 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$. From the diagram it moves at $35^{\circ}$ below the negative x-direction, so its x-component is opposite to P.
Resolve Q along x: $p_{Qx} = -p_Q \cos35^{\circ} = -8.4 \times \cos35^{\circ}$. With $\cos35^{\circ} \approx 0.819$, this is about $-6.9 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
Because P and Q form an isolated system, the total x-component of momentum is conserved through the sticking collision.
Final x-momentum = initial x-momentum = $18.0 - 6.9 \approx 11.1 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, about $11 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This subtracts the full $8.4 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ of Q without resolving it, giving $18 - 8.4 = 9.6$. Only the $\cos35^{\circ}$ part acts along P.

B.explanation: This is $18.0 - 2.0 \times 4.2\cos35^{\circ} \approx 11 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, the conserved total momentum component in the original direction of P.

C.explanation: This uses $\sin35^{\circ}$ instead of $\cos35^{\circ}$ for the component along P, giving about $13 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$. The adjacent side along P needs cosine.

D.explanation: This adds Q's forward component to P's momentum as $18.0 + 6.9 \approx 25$. Q is moving partly opposite to P, so its component must be subtracted.
